name: Edward Yellin
bio: Edward Yellin was a former Gary, Indiana steelworker and University of Illinois graduate fellow convicted of contempt of Congress and sentenced to a year in jail for refusing, at a 1958 HUAC hearing in Gary, to answer questions about his politics. His case became Yellin v. United States.
charges: Contempt of Congress — refusing to answer HUAC (Gary hearing)
convicted: Convicted and sentenced (1960); free on $1,000 bail pending appeal

name: Victor Malis
bio: Victor Malis was charged with contempt of Congress after invoking the First Amendment to refuse questions about his political beliefs and affiliations at the 1958 HUAC hearings in Gary, Indiana. His contempt trial was pending in 1960.
charges: Contempt of Congress — First Amendment refusal at the Gary HUAC hearings

name: Alfred J. Samter
bio: Alfred J. Samter was charged with contempt of Congress for invoking the First Amendment and refusing to answer questions about his political beliefs and affiliations at the 1958 HUAC hearings in Gary, Indiana. His trial was postponed indefinitely in 1960.
charges: Contempt of Congress — First Amendment refusal at the Gary HUAC hearings

name: Robert Lehrer
bio: Robert Lehrer was charged with contempt of Congress after invoking the First Amendment at the 1958 HUAC hearings in Gary, Indiana; his contempt trial, with those of Victor Malis and Alfred J. Samter, was postponed indefinitely in 1960.
charges: Contempt of Congress — First Amendment refusal at the Gary HUAC hearings

name: Maurice Ogden
bio: Maurice Ogden, a Los Angeles-area writer, was indicted in 1959 under a federal false-statements law (18 U.S.C. 1001) for allegedly misstating his organizational affiliations on a Personnel Security Questionnaire, and went on trial in July 1960 — a novel use of a statute previously applied to tax evaders to punish non-disclosure of political associations.
charges: Falsifying a federal security questionnaire (18 U.S.C. 1001) — political associations
sentence: Prosecuted for non-disclosure of political associations

name: Paul Rosenkrantz
bio: Paul Rosenkrantz was a former Communist Party member who began serving a three-month contempt-of-Congress sentence in February 1960 — described as the fourth 'First Amendment defendant' jailed in three months — for admitting his own past membership but refusing to name others before a House committee.
charges: Contempt of Congress — refusing to name fellow Communists

name: Frank Grumman
bio: Frank Grumman, a New Jersey unionist, was indicted for contempt of Congress for refusing to answer a House committee's questions about alleged Communist association. In 1960 a federal judge dismissed several of the contempt counts against him while letting others stand.
charges: Contempt of Congress — refusing to answer about Communist association

name: Bernard Silber
bio: Bernard Silber, a New York unionist, was indicted for contempt of Congress for refusing to answer a House committee's questions about Communist association. In 1960 a federal judge dismissed several of the contempt charges against him while others were left standing.
charges: Contempt of Congress — refusing to answer about Communist association

name: A. Robert Kaufman
bio: A. Robert Kaufman was a 28-year-old Baltimore socialist convicted of disorderly conduct and fined $50 for selling the newspaper Young Socialist outside a Baltimore high school. Fired as a substitute teacher and beaten by students, he appealed the conviction as an attack on free expression.
